In this case DAR was filed by the concerned police officials/IO in view of provision of Motor Vehicle Act and same is treated as petition u/s 166 MV Act, as per law. 2. Brief facts of the case are that on receiving intimation on 04.10.2020, IO reached at Nehru Place Flyover, outer Ringh Road, Delhi and found truck bearing No. HR 38V 6909 and scooty no. DL 10SW 2821 in an accidental condition. The truck driver Pramod / R-1 was also found at the spot and he told the police officer that there was some problem in his Truck and that is why he had to stop his truck on the road but the driver of the scooty mentioned above hit such standing truck and as a result of which, the driver of scooty received injury and police PCR has taken him to hospital. Further during investigation, it is claimed that no eye witness to the accident found nor any CCTV footage/ camera found regarding such place of accident. It is further claimed that R-1 during investigation confessed his involvement in the present case. MACT No. 40/21 Geeta Dangwal & Ors. Vs. Parmod & Ors. Page No. :3 : It is further stated that during investigation, ASI Satyavir joined the same and disclosed that on 04.10.2020, he was in command room, Nehru Place and they found an unknown injured/ victim lying on the road with such scooty and truck nearby. It is further stated that neither there was any reflector light at the back of such truck nor any safety equipment were found on the same. Post mortem of such deceased was conducted. 3. The police after investigation in the FIR, filed charge sheet u/s 279/304 A IPC. Present DAR was also filed by the investigating officer. 4. As per record, driver and owner appeared initially with their counsel but thereafter were irregular in appearing. 5. It is already noted that this is a case without required insurance on the date of accident as such there is no insurance company in this case. Geeta Dangwal & Ors. vs . Parmod & Ors. on 3 February, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/35902409/ 2 3) Relief. 7. Further, as per record, it is noted that in view of the Motor Vehicle Rules, 200 applicable to Delhi and Judgment by Hon'ble High Court of Delhi and Hon'ble Supreme Court regarding deposit of security amount by the owner and driver in case of no insurance accident matters, vide order dated 22.01.2021, My Ld. Predecessor issued a show cause notice to the respondents for depositing Rs. 10 lakhs in form of FDR as security amount. But from record, it appears that thereafter, MACT No. 40/21 Geeta Dangwal & Ors. Vs. Parmod & Ors. Page No. 3 of 3 :4: they neither filed their affidavit of income and assets nor gave any satisfactory reply to such show cause notice as such, vide order dated 07.08.2021, directions were issued for taking possession of such offending vehicle and accordingly same was seized on 27.10.2021 by the PS concerned and deposited in Malkhana. Thereafter R-2 filed an application recalling of seizing such offending vehicle and vide order dated 13.01.2022, my Ld. Predecessor was pleased to allow such application for stopping auction of such offending vehicle. Further the R-2 deposited Rs. 2,50,000/- in the form of FDR at that time with undertaking to deposit remaining amount. But from perusal of further ordersheet including dated 04.08.2022 ad 04.11.2022, it is noted that he failed to comply such order regarding deposit of remaining 7.5 lakhs security amount as such, it is noted in the orderhseet dated 07.11.2022 that right of such respondent is already struck off as they failed to deposit such money. As such, they were not allowed to cross examine petitioner witnesses nor allowed to lead evidence in their defence. 8. As such, although, as per record a joint reply/Written Statement along with an application praying for condonation of delay filed by the respondents side dated 24.12.2021, that is after framing of notices, same was never taken on record. 9. PW-1/petitioner no.1 (wife of deceased) tendered her examination in chief by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. She deposed that she is not eye witness to the accident but fully support the case of the prosecution. She further deposed regarding age of the deceased/ his dependants and place of work of deceased. She further relied upon certain documents in this regard Ex.PW1/A to Ex.PW1/J. 10. No other evidence was led on behalf of claimants, thereafter, PE was MACT No. 40/21 Geeta Dangwal & Ors. Vs. Parmod & Ors. 14. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. The IO has filed Detailed Accident Report before this Tribunal.
